chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Mufaddal, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'A man performs Hajj as a substitute for a man who is a substitute, and a woman performs Hajj as a substitute for a man who is a substitute.'

key_terms.الصَّرُورَةُ: the substitute / the one acting on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Hajj on behalf of a man?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the gender dynamics of Hajj substitution (Hajj al-Ni'ab), establishing that a man may perform Hajj for another man, and a woman may perform it for a man, but a woman cannot substitute for another woman. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the requirements for male and female pilgrims when acting on behalf of the deceased or those unable to perform Hajj themselves. The hadith underscores the flexibility in gender roles for Hajj substitution while maintaining specific boundaries regarding same-gender substitution for women.
